description: Reference choreography from the @zoebaptistee TikTok (two women on a bridge at night dancing the same routine in sync; the reference dancer is the creator in front on the screen-left in the lilac tracksuit, tracker id 2; 14.95 s clip, all of it dance, already trimmed before the TikTok end card at 15.0 s). Move boundaries from the wrist/elbow trajectories (hip-relative, torso-scaled), shoulder width (body turns), a self-similarity novelty curve and wrist-speed stops of data/dance/pose/zoebaptistee_200553.npz, checked against 0.1 s frame strips of data/dance/raw/zoebaptistee_200553.mp4 and data/dance/pose/zoebaptistee_200553.pose.mp4 (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema). Sides are given as seen on screen; the learner mirrors the screen.
bpm_estimate_note: Estimated, not from a track id: the song is a dembow/tresillo groove (3+3+2 sixteenths per two beats), so the rough 126 bpm estimate was a sub-beat interval, not the beat. Onset autocorrelation of the clip audio peaks at 0.479 s (125.3 bpm = 3 sixteenths, the dotted eighth inside the tresillo), 0.639 s (94 bpm), 0.798 s (75 bpm = 5 sixteenths) and 1.287 s (the two-beat tresillo cycle); an onset comb scores 2.33 x the mean at 93.5 bpm against 1.19 at 126 and 1.20 at 123. 27 strong full-band onsets fit a sixteenth-note lattice of 0.1604 s with 3.4 ms rms residual (93.5 bpm) and the sub-150 Hz 808 onsets give 93.35-93.5 bpm. The old 'first strong beat 0.62 s' is the position-3 clap/808 hit of the tresillo at 0.556 s, not a beat. The dancer agrees: her hip bounce autocorrelates at 0.633 s (one beat) and her moves change every ~1.27 s (two beats), which is 2.67 beats at 126 bpm and 1.59 at 75. Treat as 93.5 +/- 0.2 bpm, beat grid 0.075 + 0.6417k s, phrase ONEs at 2.642, 7.776 and 12.909 s.

moves.name: Talk to the hand, screen-right palm held up beside the face toward the camera with the screen-left hand on the hip, body angled to the screen-right, hips bouncing on every beat (pickup counts 5-6; the clip opens on the second half of a phrase)

Arms up into a turnaround, both arms swing up over the head toward the screen-left on count 7 as she turns her back half to the camera with a hair flip, comes back round with both hands up at the screen-right on 8, then swings them across to the screen-left on the and-of-8

Stacked-arm sit-back, the arms land out to the screen-left on count 1 and the forearms stack level in front of the chest pointing to the screen-left; side-on facing the screen-left, knees bent, hips pushed back to the screen-right, chin up, rocking the hips back on every beat through count 4

Frame the face, the forearms unfold as she squares up to the camera, both hands come up beside the face on count 5, cross in front of the chest on 6, then open out to the sides at waist height on the and-of-6

Low reach to the side, the screen-right forearm folds across the stomach with a small step on count 7, then the screen-left arm reaches out low to the screen-left, palm down, through the music stop on count 8

Punch up high, the screen-right fist snaps up beside the head on count 1, both fists tuck under the chin, the screen-right arm punches up and out to the upper screen-right on 2 and pulls back, then both hands drop to the waist, palms up, while the hips rock side to side on counts 3-4
Arms fly up overhead, both arms fling up on count 5, then the hands wave above the head with the elbows bent through count 6

Bend over to look back, the arms swing down as she turns side-on facing the screen-left, the hands land on the thighs on count 7, hips pushed back to the screen-right and bouncing on 8 while she smiles back at the camera
Turn around with arms up, the arms swing up as she spins to put her back to the camera on count 1 of the next phrase, both hands overhead with the elbows bent through count 2

Bend over the other way, the arms come down and she bends forward with the hands on the thighs on count 3, now facing the screen-right with her back to the camera and the hips pushed back to the screen-left, looking back over the shoulder and bouncing until the clip ends on count 4

notes: The clip is 449 frames (14.95 s, already trimmed before the TikTok end card at 15.0 s); the creator is tracked (ok=True, shoulders and hips visible) in all 449 frames with no gap filling, and the final move ends at the last frame (448, t=14.933 s).

Tracker id 2 is the creator in front on the screen-left (lilac tracksuit, white top). The pose json flags main_dancer_ambiguous because the second woman (black outfit and cap, track 1, also 449 frames, mean IoU 0.04 with track 2) dances the same routine for the whole clip; she is behind on the screen-right, partly overlapped, and is not the reference.

No 'ready' move: she is already dancing at frame 0 (no walk-in or idle lead-in). The first 4 counts (talk_to_hand, turnaround, 0-2.642 s) are real choreography, a pickup into the first full phrase, and play as pre-roll before count_in_s.

Beat grid 0.075 + 0.6417k s at 93.5 bpm; bars of 4 beats start at 0.075, 2.642, 5.209, 7.776, 10.342 and 12.909 s. The music alternates two bars: an F#-bass bar (sustained F#m7 pad: F# A C# E) whose 808 rests on the first half of beat 2 and on all of beat 4 (0.075, 5.209, 10.342), and a G-bass bar (Gmaj7 pad: G B D A, key D major overall) with dense bass and an octave pickup at its end (2.642, 7.776, 12.909).

Phrase ONEs are the G bars, 2.642 / 7.776 / 12.909 s, so the clip opens on count 5 of a phrase. Evidence: (1) the bass stops dead on count 8 before 2.642 and 7.776 (2.00-2.64 and 7.13-7.78 s, about -50 dB against -4 to -23 dB on the other beats), the usual stop before a ONE; (2) the 10.342 bar is the clip's one variation (the beat-2 and beat-4 rests are filled, an extra hit near 11.8 s, and the melody moves to E instead of D on its beat 3), which is the fill at the end of the 16-count group 2.642-12.909 leading into the next section at 12.909; (3) the dancer's two sharpest hits land just after the two stops (the arms land out to the screen-left at 2.60-2.70 s, the fist snaps up by the head at 7.77-7.90 s), and the turn to the back lands on 12.9 s.

Alternative considered and rejected: ONEs on the F# bars (0.075 / 5.209 / 10.342), where the clip would start on a ONE, the turn to the front (5.21) and the arms-fly-up (10.34) would land on ONE, and the 'arms up then bend' unit and its repeat to the back would sit inside one 8-count. That reading puts the full bass stop on count 4 and the fill in the first bar of a phrase. The beat grid is the same either way; only the count labels move by 4.

Lesson part: first_beat_s = count_in_s = 2.642 (bash scripts/make_dance_ref.sh zoebaptistee_200553 <name> 93.5 2.642 0.75). One 8-count is 5.134 s (6.845 s at 0.75x, which also gives 70.1 bpm and a first beat at 3.523 s). Two full 8-counts fit, 2.642-7.776 and 7.776-12.909 s, the only two complete phrases in the clip; the reference npz keeps int((14.967 - 2.642) // 5.134) = 2 chunks and the steps loop also writes 2 lines (2.642 + 2.5 x 5.134 = 15.48 > 14.933). Bullets: chunk 1 'Stacked-arm sit-back | Frame the face | Low reach to the side', chunk 2 'Punch up high | Arms fly up overhead | Bend over to look back'.

Why this window: it starts on a ONE right after a music stop and holds the dance's hook (the stacked-arm sit-back, the face frame, the punch, the arms-fly-up hit and the bend with the look back). Left out: the 4-count pickup (it still plays as pre-roll under the count-in) and the last phrase (turn around, bend the other way), which has only about 3.5 of its 8 counts in the clip. A first beat of 0.075 would also give 2 chunks, but it starts on count 5, cuts off the arms-fly-up and bend climax, and writes a 3rd steps line that the npz drops.

Move boundaries: arrivals measured from wrist speed and checked in the strips (arms overhead 1.37-1.40 s, arms land at the screen-left 2.60-2.70, fist by the head 7.77-7.90, punch extended 8.5-8.7, arms overhead 10.40-10.43, hands on the thighs 11.63, back to the camera with arms up 12.9-13.1, bent over again 14.19), and a novelty curve with a new move every ~1.27 s (peaks 1.27, 2.5, 3.7, 4.9, 6.23, 7.67, 8.9, 10.33, 11.37, 12.7, 13.8 s). punch_up includes the palms-up hip rock (8.85-10.25 s) so that each lesson chunk has exactly 3 moves, the bullet cap; otherwise the bend would be dropped from chunk 2's bullets.

The two bends mirror each other: at 11.6-12.5 s she faces the screen-left with the hips pushed back to the screen-right; at 14.2-14.9 s she faces the screen-right, back mostly to the camera, with the hips pushed back to the screen-left.

Shoulders, hips and knees are visible in every frame (mean keypoint confidence 0.89-0.99), elbows 0.90-0.92 and wrists 0.81-0.84; the ankles are below the frame edge (confidence < 0.5 in about 90% of frames), so leg faults are unreliable on this dance. The footwork is only weight shifts and small steps.
Screen-left/right in move names are image sides of the mirrored clip; with learner_mirrors_screen the learner's own right hand follows the screen-right side.
